nodes.title: Hecke action on quaternionic connected components
nodes.statement: For a sufficiently small level K of an indefinite quaternion division algebra D/F split at exactly one real place, retain every geometric connected component. Reduced norm identifies their indexing torsor with C_K=F_{f}^{×}/(F^{×,+}ν(K)). On the free finite A-module A[C_K], at v outside the discriminant, level and coefficient-action set, T_v acts by (q_v+1) times translation by the class c_v of a uniformizer, and S_v by translation by c_v². On a component character χ the spherical polynomial is (X−χ(c_v))(X−q_vχ(c_v)). This is a geometric component-action specialization of the existing GL2 Hecke normalization.
hypotheses: F totally real; D division and split at exactly one real place; K sufficiently small in the effective central quotient.
A finite coefficient algebra; the two spherical double cosets have volume(K_v)=1; translations use the right-level convention.
proofSteps: Use canonical quaternionic components and reduced-norm strong approximation to obtain the finite component torsor.
Every representative in K diag(π_v,1) K has norm class c_v, and the double coset has q_v+1 right cosets. The scalar double coset has norm class c_v².
Extend these permutations A-linearly; the character calculation agrees with IHG.3’s polynomial X²−T_vX+q_vS_v.

sources.match: The component Hecke action forces a reducible unramified characteristic polynomial.

acceptance: The action is on all components, and changing a uniformizer by a local unit does not change c_v.

nodes.title: Residual Eisenstein vanishing
nodes.statement: Let L_k be the finite k-local system from a continuous finite-image K-representation, trivial on K∩Z(F), whose action factors through finitely many finite places. Let m be a maximal ideal of the away spherical Hecke algebra with associated absolutely irreducible residual two-dimensional representation. Then H⁰(X_K,L_k)_m=H²(X_K,L_k)_m=0. The same conclusion holds for L_k∨(1) at the adjoint ideal m*. No bound on the algebraic weight relative to l is required.
hypotheses: The compact curve, level and all components satisfy component-hecke-action.
k is a finite field of characteristic l; the associated residual representation is given in the matched cohomological Hecke/Frobenius convention.
proofSteps: Trivialize L_k at a finite normal finer level. Degree-zero sections embed in component sections with fibre coefficients; their good-place Hecke characters have the reducible polynomial computed by component-hecke-action.

Use existing ray-class reciprocity (with inverse arithmetic Artin map for the stipulated geometric convention) to realize each component character as η on G_F. Its two cohomological Frobenius roots give η⊕ε⁻¹η. Chebotarev density and semisimple reconstruction contradict absolute irreducibility for a character supported at m. This is Proposition 2.4’s argument, without assuming the level quotient semisimple.
Use curve duality and the adjoint involution to transfer the degree-zero calculation for L_k∨(1) at m* to degree two for L_k at m.

sources.match: Constant and finite local coefficient cohomology in degrees zero and two has Eisenstein support.

acceptance: A residual Eisenstein ideal can have H⁰≠0; irreducibility is indispensable.
Use no idempotent averaging over a quotient of order divisible by l.

nodes.title: Adjoint Hecke localization and integral duality
nodes.statement: For finite free O-local coefficients on the compact curve, the integral Poincaré pairing pairs the m-factor of H¹(L_O) with the m*-factor of H¹(L_O∨(1)), where m* is the image of m under the anti-involution T_v*=S_v⁻¹T_v and S_v*=S_v⁻¹. Non-Eisenstein support is preserved by this involution. Under residual degree-zero vanishings on the two factors the pairing is perfect over O, and pullback is adjoint to trace. No equality m=m* is assumed.
hypotheses: O is the valuation ring of a finite extension of Q_l; the coefficients and their dual descend through the effective level.
The residual system and its adjoint factor have vanishing H⁰ as in residual-eisenstein-vanishing.
proofSteps: Identify the inverse double cosets: diag(π⁻¹,1) is centrally translated from diag(π,1), giving S⁻¹T; invert the central scalar double coset to get S⁻¹.
Apply the accepted derived cohomology-pairing and integral-cohomology-control to these two localized factors.
After residual vanishings eliminate adjacent-degree obstructions, derived duality restricts to a perfect degree-one lattice pairing. The trace identity follows from generic finite-level duality.

sources.match: The Hecke adjoint involution relates degrees zero and two.
Curve duality and the trace normalization are compatible.

acceptance: A central character of order greater than two can have m*≠m; the target retains both factors.
The degree-one pairing is integral only after the stated vanishings.

nodes.title: Non-Eisenstein integral cohomology control
nodes.statement: For the finite free O-local system L_O on X_K and a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal m as above, H⁰(L_O)_m=H²(L_O)_m=0, H¹(L_O)_m is finite free over O, and H¹(L_O)_m⊗_O k→H¹(L_k)_m is an isomorphism. For every n≥1 the analogous O/λⁿ coefficient reduction is an isomorphism. These statements apply at both hyperspecial and sufficiently small Iwahori levels with coefficients descending there.
hypotheses: All localized cohomology groups are finite O-modules as in the accepted finite-cohomology node.
Finite free coefficients and their residual dual satisfy residual-eisenstein-vanishing.
proofSteps: Apply residual-eisenstein-vanishing to L_k and its Tate dual, keeping the adjoint ideal.
The coefficient exact sequence and Nakayama kill H²(L_O)_m; degree-zero torsion-free sections vanish by reduction.

The same sequence makes H¹(L_O)_m λ-torsion-free. Apply the accepted control node and the pinned PID finite-torsion-free freeness result. Induct on n using coefficient sequences to obtain every finite reduction.

sources.match: Residual Eisenstein vanishing supplies the finite-level integral reduction needed for homology and cohomology.
Duality controls the adjacent degree in the coefficient sequence.

acceptance: The proof applies to all n, not merely rational coefficients.
No corresponding unqualified freeness assertion is made for an open Hilbert variety.

nodes.title: Finite-cover reduction for Ihara coefficients
nodes.statement: Let H^w be an open normal subgroup of K^w trivializing a finite k-representation Λ of K^w, trivial on K∩Z(F). At a non-Eisenstein ideal, injectivity of the constant-coefficient degeneracy map at every sufficiently small finer H^w implies injectivity for L_Λ at K. The quotient K^w/H^w may have order divisible by l.
hypotheses: The degeneracy prime w is split for D and K_w is hyperspecial.
The coefficient action is away from w; the same normal subgroup is used at both w-levels.
proofSteps: Use the finite-cover Hochschild–Serre sequence, not division by the covering degree.
Its initial H¹(Δ,H⁰(X_H,k)⊗Λ) term vanishes after non-Eisenstein localization by residual-eisenstein-vanishing; H⁰ itself vanishes there.
Identify H¹ at K with the Δ-invariants of the localized finer cohomology tensored with Λ. An equivariant injective degeneracy map remains injective after invariants.

sources.match: Finite local coefficients reduce to constant coefficients by Hochschild–Serre and degree-zero vanishing.

acceptance: A cover quotient of l-power order is an acceptance case; averaging is unavailable.
Coefficients acting nontrivially at w are outside this reduction.

nodes.title: Arithmetic coefficient adapter for twisted Betti cohomology
nodes.statement: For a finite free O-representation W of the arithmetic component group, the ordinary Betti local system L_W is compared with Tau Ceti’s existing twisted cochain complex applied to L_(W∨) and target O: its cochains take Hom_O(W∨,O), identified with W by biduality. This yields H^i_B(X_K,L_W), naturally for coefficient maps, level pullback and Hecke trace. Applying the existing complex to L_W itself would compute dual coefficients.
hypotheses: Finite free fibres; effective small level; all arithmetic components and the prescribed local coefficient action retained.
The algebraic sheaf/Betti comparison is imported from the accepted arithmetic local-system and sheaf-singular comparison nodes.
proofSteps: Read the actual twisted complex: it is linear Yoneda applied to twisted chains and is contravariant in its coefficient local system.
Use fibrewise finite-projective biduality to identify Hom(W∨,O) with W, with transport carried by the dual inverse action.
Apply ALS.1/sheaf-singular-comparison; verify naturality under pullback and the stalk-sum trace rather than construct another generic twisted cohomology theory.

sources.match: Arithmetic representations define local systems on quaternionic components.
Finite local coefficient étale/Betti comparison is compatible with the sheaf interpretation.

acceptance: For W rank one with monodromy a unit u, the adapted coefficient transport is u; the unadapted Hom complex has u⁻¹.
Current Tau Ceti twisted declarations are credited at current main, without claiming their presence at the old pin.

nodes.title: Finite-level Hilbert support comparison
nodes.statement: For a smooth finite-level Hilbert modular variety Y over a number field, algebraic integral coefficients from the accepted Hilbert arithmetic local-system construction, and an embedding into C, finite O/λⁿ étale and Betti cohomology agree naturally in every degree, with ordinary and compact supports and the map H_c^i→H^i. Passing to compatible O-adic systems gives their derived integral comparison. Inner cohomology is the image of this support map; its rational Hecke eigenspaces use ALS.5. No compactness, integral torsion-freeness or degree-g concentration is inferred.
hypotheses: The level is small enough for a smooth scheme or the declared effective groupoid treatment; coefficients are genuinely defined on both sides.
Support comparisons, constructible extension by zero and inverse-system hypotheses are those of CC.0’s imported comparison target.
proofSteps: Specialize the arithmetic-local-system and level-pullback nodes to the Hilbert space, using the bidual adapter for existing Betti complexes.
Import the finite étale/Betti support and trace-orientation comparisons from CC.0; take the compatible derived O-adic system.
Define the inner groups by the actual image of H_c→H and use functoriality to transport Hecke actions; the geometric boundary is not discarded.

sources.match: Finite local coefficient comparison extends to constructible support calculations.
Inner cohomology is the image between the two support theories, not the entire ordinary group.

acceptance: An open Hilbert surface retains the support map and boundary contribution.
Generic constructible comparison is a supplier target with its recorded gaps; this arithmetic adapter does not silently close them.

nodes.title: GL2 degeneracy Gram operator
nodes.statement: For a commutative Hecke coefficient algebra A acting on an A-module M, q∈N, T∈A and S∈A×, define G_(q,T,S) on M⊕M by (x,y)↦((q+1)x+S⁻¹Ty,Tx+(q+1)y). Put Δ=(q+1)²−S⁻¹T² and J(x,y)=((q+1)x−S⁻¹Ty,−Tx+(q+1)y). Then GJ=JG=Δ id. The chosen ordering corresponds to T=π₂,*π₁*.
hypotheses: All scalar operations use the actual commuting Hecke image; S is a unit, not tacitly one.
proofSteps: Form the A-linear product map using scalar endomorphisms and the displayed four entries.
Expand compositions to get the scalar Δ; commutativity cancels mixed terms.
Match the central involution T*=S⁻¹T in the geometry below.

sources.match: Right-level maps and double cosets determine the two trace-pullback entries; the matrix is derived here with the central adjoint retained.

acceptance: The definition specializes to the symmetric PGL2 matrix only after S acts as one.

nodes.title: Geometric degeneracy Gram identity
nodes.statement: At a split hyperspecial prime w, take ω=diag(π_w,1), K_0(w) with lower-left entry divisible by π_w, π₁=ρ_1 and π₂=ρ_(ω⁻¹). Both maps X_(K_0(w))→X_K have degree q_w+1. For coefficients acted on away from w, δ=π₁*+π₂*:M²→M_0 and δ†=(π₁,*,π₂,*). With T_w=π₂,*π₁* and S_w the central scalar double coset, δ†δ=G_(q_w,T_w,S_w).
hypotheses: Use the maps and coefficient identifications of the accepted cohomological-degeneracy node.
All cohomology is localized at an away Hecke ideal compatible with these maps; integral traces have their unnormalized degree convention.
proofSteps: Count cosets for both maps, obtaining diagonal trace-pullback q_w+1.
The composite π₂,*π₁* is the diag(π_w,1) double coset in the stipulated right-action convention.
The reverse composite is its inverse double coset, centrally translated by S_w⁻¹. Substitute the four entries in degeneracy-gram.

sources.match: The two right-level degeneracy maps and the central spherical operator fix the normalization.

acceptance: Changing the ordering of π₁ and π₂ transposes the off-diagonal entries; the declared ordering remains fixed.
The double-coset identity holds before assuming residual Ihara.

nodes.title: Unit-discriminant oldspace splitting
nodes.statement: If Δ=(q_w+1)²−S_w⁻¹T_w² is a unit in the localized Hecke image, then r=Δ⁻¹Jδ† is an integral left inverse of δ. Thus the old module im δ is a direct summand of M_0 and δ is injective. With free M_0 the quotient is O-free. The hypothesis Δ∈A× is sufficient for this splitting, not necessary for Ihara saturation.
hypotheses: geometric-gram-identity; all scalar operators commute and Δ is a unit.
The freeness conclusion additionally assumes O a DVR and M_0 finite free.
proofSteps: Use the adjugate identity to compute rδ=Δ⁻¹JG=id.
The idempotent δr gives M_0=im δ⊕ker r.
Finite direct summands of a free DVR module are finite torsion-free and hence free.

sources.match: The trace and degeneracy operators supply the input; this unit-discriminant conclusion is an explicit algebraic deduction.

acceptance: Δ≡0 mod λ does not prove failure of residual Ihara; no converse is asserted.
The left inverse contains the central operator in J.

nodes.title: Residual injectivity and DVR saturation
nodes.statement: For a DVR O with uniformizer λ, finite free O-modules M,N and an O-linear f:M→N, injectivity of f mod λ is equivalent to f being injective with finite free cokernel. Equivalently f is injective and im f is saturated in N. Here saturated means λy∈im f implies y∈im f; all nonzero scalars then have the same property.
hypotheses: O is a nonfield DVR; λ generates its maximal ideal; M and N are finite free.
proofSteps: If f mod λ is injective, divide a purported kernel vector by its minimal coordinate valuation to contradict reduction.
If λy=f(x), reduction gives x=λx′; torsion-freeness of N gives y=f(x′). Thus the cokernel has no λ-torsion, hence no torsion. Apply the pinned finite-torsion-free freeness theorem.
Conversely a short exact sequence with a free cokernel stays exact after tensoring k, so f mod λ is injective.

sources.match: The residual theorem is intended for integral localized modules; the equivalence here is the separate DVR algebra needed to deduce saturation.

acceptance: Multiplication by λ on O is injective but has nonsaturated image and zero residual map.
The assertion needs both source and target free; rational injectivity alone is insufficient.

nodes.title: Auxiliary unipotent prime
nodes.statement: Suppose l>2, ρ̄:G_F→GL₂(k) is absolutely irreducible with finite image whose order is divisible by l. Outside any prescribed finite set there is a split good prime q with Nq≡1 mod l and ρ̄(Frob_q) conjugate to a nonidentity unipotent matrix. This auxiliary prime is distinct from the Taylor–Wiles primes with distinct residual eigenvalues.
hypotheses: F totally real; k a finite field of characteristic l; extend k to contain the matrix entries.
The excluded set contains l, the discriminant, all level and coefficient-action primes, and the intended degeneracy prime w.
proofSteps: Cauchy’s theorem gives an element of order l in the residual image; in dimension two it is a nonidentity unipotent, conjugate to J=(1,1;0,1).
In a finite extension containing the splitting field and F(ζ_l), lift this element to σ₀ and take σ=σ₀^(1−l). Its residual matrix remains J and its cyclotomic character becomes one.
Apply number-field Chebotarev to this conjugacy class. Inverting Frobenius changes to a conjugate nonidentity unipotent and leaves Nq≡1 intact.

sources.match: Chebotarev jointly prescribes a unipotent residual element and trivial residual cyclotomic value.

acceptance: Requiring two distinct residual eigenvalues at this q would contradict its role.
For an exceptional residual image this argument does not produce q.

nodes.title: Local deformation models for quaternionic Ihara
nodes.statement: For the auxiliary q, residual unramified J and fixed determinant θ=ψε⁻¹, choose O=W(k)[ζ+ζ⁻¹] with ζ a primitive lth root and π=(ζ−ζ⁻¹)². The q-local fixed-determinant quotients are R_ps=O[[X,Y₁,P,R]]/(X²Y₁−π), R_unip=O[[X,Y₂,P,R]]/(XY₂), R_nr=R_unip/(X) and R_N=R_unip/(Y₂). Their residual coordinates identify Y₁=Y₂=Y, with k[[X,Y,P,R]]/(X²Y)→k[[X,Y,P,R]]/(XY). At v|l use the O-flat reduced potentially semistable quotient over the specified finite extension L′/F_v, parallel Hodge–Tate weights {0,1} and determinant θ; its nonempty components have dimension 3+[F_v:Q_l]. At v∤l unrestricted fixed-determinant framed rings are O-flat of relative dimension 3.
hypotheses: l>2; at q the finite-order ψ is unramified and det ρ̄=ψε⁻¹ mod π.
O has the stated minimal ramification during the regular-model flatness argument. Unrestricted coefficient enlargement is made only after the argument by faithful flatness.
At v|l choose L′ making the finite set of local Weil–Deligne types with the prescribed K_v⁰ invariants semistable and trivializing ψ there.
proofSteps: Apply the generic framed representability node, using local finite Galois cohomology for the finiteness hypothesis, then impose determinant θ.

At q impose the inertia characteristic polynomials and the unipotent level-raising relation of MS §3.3. In its coordinates eliminate the determinant variable δ. Propositions 3.5–3.7 give the four-variable presentations and the common residual coordinate.

R_ps is regular because its defining equation has uniformizer term; R_nr and R_N are formal power-series rings. For v|l the precise quotient is the Zariski closure of the allowed characteristic-zero points. Its representability/dimension proof is retained as the local-deformation source gap, not inferred from a predicate on points.

sources.match: Fixed determinant eliminates one coordinate and yields the regular principal-series and nodal unipotent models; §3.2 cites Kisin for the p-adic quotient.

acceptance: The exact special-fibre thickening is X²Y, not XY; the flatness transfer needs this difference.

nodes.title: Early quaternionic local type correspondence
nodes.statement: At q∤l with q≡1 mod l and residual unramified J, local Langlands in the cohomological normalization and local Jacquet–Langlands give the following characteristic-zero support criteria for the prescribed determinant: spherical/trivial type implies R_nr; Steinberg type implies R_unip; a discrete-series representation compatible with the q-ramified quaternion algebra implies R_N; the principal-series inertial type χ⊕χ⁻¹ for an order-l tame character χ implies R_ps. For the definite module only the discrete-series alternative occurs. These are factorization assertions for actual cohomological Galois actions, not equivalences for every deformation.
hypotheses: Inflate the finite GL₂(k_q) types to GL₂(O_q), with central character compatible with ψ.
The underlying Weil–Deligne representation is that of the early quaternionic cohomological realization, with geometric reciprocity and its specified dual/twist.
proofSteps: For spherical vectors inertia is trivial. Steinberg and principal-series types are detected by their inertia polynomial and the Frobenius/monodromy relation; substitute the defining conditions of MS §3.3.
The q-ramified quaternion algebra matches precisely discrete-series GL₂ representations via local Jacquet–Langlands, so use its N branch.

Apply local-global compatibility at q∤l to the actual cohomology representations. The integral factorization follows from O-flatness and the scheme-theoretic characteristic-zero closures in the local models.

sources.match: The geometric cohomological Weil–Deligne normalization and prime-to-l local compatibility are specified.

nodes.title: Finite-level Taylor–Wiles prime datum
nodes.statement: For the large-image residual representation and exceptional l=5 condition of residual-ihara-large-image, fix finite S and local conditions as above. With Σ the framed finite places, j=4|Σ|−1, there exist integers r,g and sets Q_n outside S, |Q_n|=r, with Nv≡1 mod lⁿ and two distinct residual Frobenius eigenvalues at v∈Q_n. Choose one eigenvalue at each v. The framed fixed-determinant global ring R_(S∪Q_n)^□,θ admits a surjection R_loc[[x₁,…,x_g]]→R_(S∪Q_n)^□,θ. The unframed ring represents strict-equivalence deformations with the same determinant θ, and framing is formally smooth of relative dimension j. Set R_∞=R_loc[[x₁,…,x_g]] and S_∞=O[[y₁,…,y_r,w₁,…,w_j]]; dim R_loc=r+j−g+1 and dim R_∞=dim S_∞=r+j+1.
hypotheses: ρ̄|_(G_F(ζ_l)) absolutely irreducible; for l=5 with projective image PGL₂(F₅), ker proj ρ̄ is not contained in G_F(ζ₅).
Finite-order ψ trivial on the central level, θ=ψε⁻¹, and exactly the same θ for framed and unframed functors.
The local deformation models and global ramification set satisfy MS §4.2, with Σ containing all l-adic places and auxiliary q.
proofSteps: Use arithmetic Galois finiteness and generic representability to construct the global fixed-determinant strict and framed functors. Absolute irreducibility removes noncentral infinitesimal automorphisms, giving j frame parameters.

The adjoint Selmer/dual Selmer calculation selects r Taylor–Wiles primes with chosen distinct eigenvalues and kills the dual Selmer obstruction. This exact arithmetic selection theorem is requested from lower-tier Selmer cohomology.
Apply the generic minimal-presentation and relation-bound algebra to obtain the uniform surjections and the displayed numerical dimension equality, as in MS Lemma 4.10.

sources.match: Taylor–Wiles primes, global framed presentations and matching numerical dimensions are available under these image hypotheses.

acceptance: The auxiliary q has repeated eigenvalues; Q_n has distinct eigenvalues and excludes q.
A framed ring with determinant θ cannot map by forgetting frames to an unframed ring with determinant ψ.

nodes.title: Early finite-level quaternionic Galois–Hecke realization
nodes.statement: For the compact quaternionic curve with constant weight-two coefficients, a non-Eisenstein ideal m and a finite-order central character ψ lifting det ρ̄·ε, the localized O-flat Hecke image acting on H¹ carries a continuous two-dimensional representation ρ_T of G_(F,S). In geometric Frobenius conventions det(X−ρ_T(Frob_v))=X²−T_vX+q_vS_v at v∉S and det ρ_T=ψε⁻¹. At v|l it satisfies the specified K_v⁰-potentially semistable weight-{0,1} condition. Consequently the unframed fixed-θ global ring surjects onto this Hecke image, compatibly with finer levels; the separate local-type target supplies the q-type factorization. A residual irreducible representation is an input to localization; no modularity-lifting theorem is used.
hypotheses: The cohomology module is finite free by non-eisenstein-integral-control and the Hecke image is the actual image on it.
Coefficient field enlarged to split residual ρ̄; ψ-central part treated by central-character-exactness.
proofSteps: Decompose the characteristic-zero cohomology using the accepted eigenspace construction and the minimal Jacquet–Langlands bridge. Carayol’s geometric realization supplies prime-to-l local compatibility and the spherical polynomials.

Interpolate the two-dimensional determinants into the O-flat integral Hecke image using IHG.4/compact-determinant-gluing, then IHG.1/continuous-matrix-reconstruction at the split absolutely irreducible residue.
Use finite-level p-adic compatibility to factor through the l-adic local quotients; this step does not follow from Carayol’s prime-to-l theorem and is recorded as an unresolved source proof input.
The universal property supplies R^θ→T; it is surjective because the away Frobenius traces generate the Hecke image. Use Chebotarev for uniqueness and level compatibility.

sources.match: The pre-patching global deformation ring acts through the localized Hecke algebra, with local conditions established before patching.
Compact quaternionic cohomology realizes the prime-to-l compatible system.

acceptance: This is the minimal input formerly sought from R19.2; it has no prerequisite in R22.
Arithmetic Frobenius uses the normalized reciprocal polynomial; the stated q_vS_v determinant is geometric.

nodes.title: Exact central-character localization
nodes.statement: Let Γ_K=Z(A_f)/(Z(F)(K∩Z(A_f))) act effectively on the sufficiently small compact curve, and let A be a finite local Z_l-algebra. The localized dual cohomology H¹(X_K,A)∨_m and definite function module H⁰(Y_K,A)∨_m are injective A[Γ_K]-modules. Therefore their ψ-isotypical functor and corresponding homological character quotient are exact on the finite-level modules and filtrations under consideration, including when l divides |Γ_K|. This supplies the exact central-character steps used by the patching system.
hypotheses: m non-Eisenstein; ψ compatible with the central level and coefficients.
Smallness makes the finite central quotient action free, not just an action of an ineffective center.
proofSteps: Apply the finite-cover Hochschild–Serre sequence to the free central quotient action. Degrees zero and two vanish after non-Eisenstein localization.
The resulting cohomological concentration proves the localized dual is injective over A[Γ_K], as in MS Lemma 2.5. The definite function module is obtained from free finite orbits.
Use injectivity and the dual quotient functor to take ψ-parts of the particular sequences; use Nakayama in the finite central group algebra to remove the chosen character in the final Ihara argument.

sources.locator: §2.12 and Lemma 2.5, pp.10–11; end of proof of Theorem 6.5, p.38
sources.match: Central-character extraction is exact by injectivity, and the final character reduction is removed by Nakayama.

acceptance: A central quotient with l-torsion is allowed; the proof does not divide by its order.
This statement concerns the localized arithmetic modules, not arbitrary A[Γ_K]-modules.

nodes.title: Auxiliary-prime integral types
nodes.statement: Let G_q=GL₂(k_q), B_q its upper Borel, q≡1 mod l, l>2 and O as in the local-model node. The permutation representation Ind_(B_q)^(G_q)1 splits over O as 1⊕St_O, where St_O is the sum-zero complement (q+1 is a unit). Choose a tame character χ:k_q×→O[ζ]× of exact order l. The characteristic-zero type σ_ps=Ind(χ⊗χ⁻¹) has an E-model by its Schur-index/descent result and an O-lattice with residual nonsplit sequence 0→1_k→σ_ps,k→St_k→0. Fix this orientation of the lattice; the reverse extension is not interchangeable. Inflate all types through GL₂(O_q)→G_q.
hypotheses: The chosen E is the fraction field of W(k)[ζ+ζ⁻¹]; scalar extension to E(ζ) defines the inducing characters.
Prescribed central character is unramified at q, so its restriction to GL₂(O_q) matches the types.
proofSteps: Construct the permutation representation on P¹(k_q); average only its q+1 basis coordinates, which is permissible since q+1 is a unit.

Descend the self-inverse principal-series type from E(ζ) by its finite-group Schur-index theorem. Choose a lattice whose socle is 1_k using the specified nonsplit-extension lattice theorem. These two finite representation-theory proofs are a precise SR.3 Part II request.
Reduce the chosen lattice; the order-l characters become trivial but the lattice reduction is the nonsplit extension, rather than a semisimple direct sum.

sources.match: The principal-series lattice has a residual extension with trivial submodule and Steinberg quotient; the permutation representation splits integrally.
An irreducible residually multiplicity-free representation has a unique lattice up to homothety with a prescribed simple socle or cosocle.

acceptance: dim St=q and dim σ_ps=q+1; orientation of the residual extension is part of the construction.

nodes.title: Supersingular cohomology filtration
nodes.statement: At the auxiliary q, the smooth proper hyperspecial integral model and regular Iwahori model have special fibre consisting of two copies of the hyperspecial curve meeting transversely at supersingular points. The supersingular set is Hecke-equivariantly identified with the definite quaternionic double-coset set for the inner form ramified at the original discriminant together with q and the split real place. After non-Eisenstein localization, H¹(X_(K_0(q)),k) has a functorial Hecke-module filtration with graded pieces N, M⊕M, N, where M=H¹(X_K,k) and N=H⁰(Y_(K^q),k). The ψ-parts and dual homology filtration remain exact. This statement forgets Galois action; no unstated Tate twists are assigned to the graded pieces.
hypotheses: q∤l and outside level/discriminant; sufficiently small level and good integral models.
The auxiliary residual unipotent Frobenius and non-Eisenstein ideal satisfy the hypotheses of the specialization filtration.
proofSteps: Specialize the accepted regular-model tower at the new split q. The two components and finite étale/supersingular correspondence are MS Theorems 2.6 and 2.10.

Use the normalization and vanishing-cycle exact sequences and the degree-zero/degree-two vanishings to identify the remaining degree-one filtration. The proper curve specialization and nodal vanishing-cycle sequence are imported from LPV.7:semistable-curves.
Use central-character-exactness and finite-dimensional duality to transfer the filtration to the actual homological modules with transition and degeneracy maps.

nodes.title: Quaternionic Ihara patching functor
nodes.statement: Build the ordinary finite-level type functor σ↦M_∞(σ) from the full localized H¹ dual at auxiliary Taylor–Wiles levels, and the definite functor N_∞. At Q_n use Δ_n, the product of maximal l-power residue-field multiplicative quotients, and chosen U_v eigenvalues. The finite-level homology modules are finite free over O[Δ_n], with augmentation identifying them with the base-level modules. Frame with j variables and patch over S_∞ to R_∞. M_∞ is exact on finite σ, has the prescribed augmentation M_∞(σ)⊗_(S_∞)O=M_0(σ), and is maximal Cohen–Macaulay on its local-type ring for free σ, and modulo π for residual σ. Patch the N,M²,N filtration compatibly. The full two-dimensional cohomological Galois multiplicity is retained; the functor is not a multiplicity-one module. For a finite torsion type σ, its dual means Hom_O(σ,E/O). For a free integral type use the compatible finite σ/λⁿ systems and inverse limit to obtain an O-free homology dual, not Hom_O(H¹(O),E/O) treated as O-free.
hypotheses: Use the Taylor–Wiles datum, early Galois–Hecke action, local type support and exact central-character parts at every level.
The generic patching theorem must expose cofinal ideals I_n=((1+y_i)^(l^(e_ni))−1), e_ni≥n, matched dimensions and maximal Cohen–Macaulay quotients in each exact patched sequence.
The residual filtration is patched only under the exactness hypotheses of MS Lemma 4.7; arbitrary inverse-limit patching is not asserted exact.
proofSteps: Form the fine levels as kernels of the residue-field quotient at Q_n; localize U_v at the chosen residual eigenvalues and prove the O[Δ_n] freeness and augmentation isomorphisms from the finite-level cover action and non-Eisenstein concentration.
Adjoin frame variables and apply the imported R03.5 patching datum, with the requested exactness extension. Equidimensional numerical equality and finite-level freeness produce MCM modules.
For a finite type σ use the arithmetic local coefficient sheaf of σ∨ in cohomology, dualize and patch; pass compatibly through σ/πⁿ for integral free types.
Patch the filtration using MCM residual graded quotients; use the early local type theorem to factor each action through R_nr, R_unip, R_ps or R_N.

sources.locator: Lemma 4.7, p.21; Propositions 4.14 and 4.16, pp.26–27; Theorems 4.17 and 4.19, pp.28–29; Propositions 4.20–4.21, p.30
sources.match: The finite-level systems patch with exactness, augmentation, MCM and local support under these hypotheses.

acceptance: All specialization maps recover the full finite-level homology modules and commute with the w-degeneracy traces.

nodes.title: Patched Steinberg branch flatness
nodes.statement: With the preceding finite-level patching datum, M_∞(1) is flat over R_nr, N_∞ is flat over R_N and M_∞(σ_ps,O) is flat over the regular R_ps. Residually M_∞(St_k) is flat over B=k[[X,Y]]/(XY) (with the retained formal smooth parameters), M_∞(St_k)/X≅M_∞(1_k), and there is an exact sequence 0→N_∞→M_∞(St_k)/Y→N_∞→0. All identifications are R_∞-linear and commute with the w-degeneracy maps.
hypotheses: The local rings are precisely the minimal-ramification models above, and the nonzero modules have the stated MCM dimension equality.
The type sequence and N,M²,N filtration are exact and compatible; zero modules are treated as flat separately.
proofSteps: Apply R03.3/miracle-flatness-finite-modules to the regular local bases R_nr,R_N,R_ps, checking the relative dimension equality from the actual patched local tensor product.
Use the requested MS Lemma 5.2 algebra: over A=k[[X,Y]]/(X²Y), an exact 0→L→M→N→0 with M A-flat, XL=0, XYN=0 yields N=M/(XY)M flat over B and N/XN≅L.

Apply the requested Lemma 5.3 algebra to M=M_∞(St_k), L=M/XM, the Iwahori decomposition P=L⊕M and its N,L²,N filtration. Its hypotheses include N flat over B/(Y). Obtain the stated exact sequence modulo Y.

sources.match: Regular-base flatness and the two nodal transfer lemmas yield the Steinberg branch identities.

All smooth framing factors survive; the fixed-determinant q-local core has four variables.

nodes.title: Patched degeneracy surjectivity
nodes.statement: For constant residual coefficients and the large-image datum, the homological trace map M_∞,K_0(w)(St_k)→M_∞,K(St_k)² is surjective. Specializing by X and then the S_∞ augmentation gives the surjective finite-level trace H₁(X_(K_0(w)),k)_m→H₁(X_K,k)_m², first on the chosen central character and then on the whole localized module.
hypotheses: The patched-type-flatness exact sequences are constructed at K and K_0(w) compatibly.
The target source levels at w are small and hyperspecial/Iwahori, and definite Ihara is available from R18.3.
proofSteps: Form the commuting two-row short exact diagram modulo Y with outer terms N_∞ and N_∞². Definite Ihara makes the two outer trace maps surjective after augmentation.

The finite patched cokernels vanish by Nakayama; the short exact diagram then makes the middle map modulo Y surjective. Apply Nakayama again with Y in the maximal ideal to get the full Steinberg map surjective.
Tensor with the unramified branch X=0, using patched-type-flatness, then specialize S_∞ to k. Remove the central character quotient by the finite central-algebra Nakayama argument.

sources.match: A compatible exact diagram transfers definite trace surjectivity to the curve through the two branch specializations.

acceptance: Use surjectivity of finite cokernels and Nakayama; no exactness of tensoring an arbitrary short exact sequence is assumed.
The proof never uses an R=T theorem or R22 patching outcome.

nodes.title: Large-image residual Ihara lemma
nodes.statement: Let l>2, D/F a quaternion division algebra split at exactly one real place, K sufficiently small and hyperspecial at a split finite place w, and Λ a finite k-representation of K^w trivial on the rational central stabilizers. Let m be non-Eisenstein with absolutely irreducible ρ̄_m. Assume l divides |ρ̄_m(G_F)|. If l=5 and proj ρ̄_m(G_F)≅PGL₂(F₅), assume ker proj ρ̄_m is not contained in G_F(ζ₅). Then δ:H¹_et(X_K,L_Λ)_m²→H¹_et(X_(K_0(w)),L_Λ)_m is injective. The exceptional condition is automatic if √5∉F. The theorem allows w|l only when the coefficient action is away from w. It makes no assertion for l=2 or the exceptional small images.
hypotheses: All coefficient and effective smallness hypotheses above; the same away Hecke ideal is used at both levels.
proofSteps: Choose the auxiliary unipotent q and the minimal coefficient ring. Construct the Taylor–Wiles systems and their local-type patching functor without modularity lifting.
Apply patched-degeneracy-surjectivity and finite-dimensional duality to get constant residual cohomological injectivity.
Use coefficient-descent-for-ihara to extend to Λ; descend or extend the finite coefficient field by faithful flatness.

sources.locator: Theorem 6.5 and Remarks 6.6–6.7, p.34; proof, p.38
sources.match: The residual Ihara result has the large-image and l=5 Taylor–Wiles hypotheses, and is proved for arbitrary finite coefficients away from w.

acceptance: The statement does not replace the large-image condition by absolute irreducibility alone.
The local coefficient factorization at w must be checked even when w lies over l.
Proof closure requires the two explicitly recorded p-adic source inputs and the exact lower-tier requested contracts; these are proof leaves, not additional image hypotheses.

nodes.title: Integral Ihara saturation
nodes.statement: Under residual-ihara-large-image, let L_O be a finite free O-lattice system with reduction Λ and coefficient action away from w. Then δ:H¹_et(X_K,L_O)_m²→H¹_et(X_(K_0(w)),L_O)_m is injective and its image is saturated; the cokernel is finite free over O. It remains so after extending O and after reduction to O/λⁿ. This is an integral consequence of the residual theorem and the established control isomorphisms; it is independent of Δ being a unit.
hypotheses: The localized source and target have the finite-free and reduction statements of non-eisenstein-integral-control.
All image, smallness and coefficient hypotheses of the residual theorem hold.
proofSteps: Identify reduction of the integral degeneracy map with the residual map by functorial cohomology control.
Apply residual-ihara-large-image and residual-injectivity-saturation to obtain injectivity and finite-free cokernel.
Tensor the resulting split short exact sequence of finite-free DVR modules to any coefficient extension or O/λⁿ.

sources.locator: Theorem 6.5, p.34, with §2.10 and Lemma 6.4, pp.10,34
sources.match: Residual injectivity and local coefficient control are the inputs; saturation is derived here by the stated DVR criterion.

acceptance: A level-raising ideal with Δ≡0 is still allowed by Ihara.
The result is not asserted for arbitrary integral weights that act nontrivially at w.

nodes.title: Early quaternionic Jacquet–Langlands bridge
nodes.statement: For quaternion inner forms of GL₂ over F, the non-character discrete automorphic spectrum transfers, with multiplicity one, to the cuspidal GL₂ spectrum whose components at every ramified place are discrete series. Away from ramification the local factors and unnormalized Hecke eigenvalues agree; at ramified places use local Jacquet–Langlands. In particular, exchanging the unique split real place τ and a split finite place q changes an indefinite algebra to a definite one, and the common characteristic-zero eigensystems are exactly those for which π_q is discrete series. With an actual common field E of definition, compare the corresponding multiplicity spaces, not all H¹ with all H⁰ and not integral lattices. For the same spherical Hecke algebra away from q and the other bad places, the q-definite Hecke image is consequently a quotient of the q-Iwahori indefinite characteristic-zero Hecke image; finite torsion-free integral images inherit the kernel inclusion.
hypotheses: F a number field, fixed compatible central character and the indicated quaternion inner forms.
Exclude characters of D× and the corresponding noncuspidal discrete GL₂ representations; use actual rational models, not a chosen embedding C alone.
proofSteps: Use AF.3’s discrete cuspidal spectrum and the local discrete-series character correspondence. The required quaternion trace comparison is requested from AS.6, with matching orbital integrals at the ramified places.
Apply BR Theorem 18.1 to obtain the global transfer, multiplicity one and common unramified factors. For GL₂ the only noncuspidal discrete alternatives are the excluded character transfers.
At τ and q impose the two local compatibilities, then use the accepted definite and indefinite coefficient realizations and AF.4 rational models to compare E-multiplicity spaces.
For the kernel inclusion used in patching, tensor both finite torsion-free integral modules with E, obtain the inclusion by the common eigensystems, then descend the zero action by torsion-freeness.

sources.match: The global inner-form correspondence identifies the compatible discrete spectra and proves multiplicity one through trace comparison.
The definite Hecke action factors through the indefinite action at q-Iwahori level by Jacquet–Langlands and integral torsion-freeness.

acceptance: A π_q principal series is excluded from the q-ramified definite side.
A rank-two Galois factor in H¹ prevents an unqualified H⁰≅H¹ statement.

nodes.title: Saito quaternionic coefficient projector
nodes.statement: Let g=[F:Q], k=(k_i,w) with k_i≥2, all k_i≡w mod 2 and w≥max_i k_i. Use Saito’s actual CM/PEL bridge M×N→M″ and CM elliptic family A₀→N₀, not an elliptic family on M. After a splitting coefficient field L, the PEL endomorphism algebra is a product of two M₂(L) factors at each i; select the indicated second/conjugate factor and a rank-one matrix idempotent e_i. Its action on R¹a_*L_λ has rank two. Degree-one, Young/symmetric/determinant and CM projectors produce X=α*A^{g(w−2)}×β*A₀^{a}, a=(g−1)(w−2), and an L-linear algebraic correspondence e. Write q₀=(2g−1)(w−2). The only nonzero projected R^j c_* is j=q₀, with eR^q₀c_*=pr₁*F(k)⊗β*F(χ₀)^a. Here F(χ₀), after forgetting the torus action, has Tate type L_λ(−1). Leray yields eH^j(X_Ē,L_λ)≅H^{j−q₀}(M_F̄,F(k))⊗H⁰(N_Ē,F(χ₀)^a), G_E- and Hecke-equivariantly. Selecting an actual CM eigensummand L_λ(−a) identifies the selected degree-(q₀+1) factor with H¹(M,F(k))(−a).
hypotheses: Small compatible levels and stable lattices admit the stated PEL and CM abelian schemes and maps α,β; the effective descent is part of the accepted coefficient system.
All determinant exponents (w−k_i)/2 are nonnegative; rational idempotents have denominators, so exclude their support for an integral action.
At the good reduction prime p use the extension of the abelian schemes and prime-to-p correspondences in Saito Lemma 4; λ∤p.

For the invoked semistable-model form of Saito Lemma 4, choose a further sufficiently small level with every geometric curve component of genus greater than one; at a good smooth model the same correspondence extension applies directly.
proofSteps: Use the accepted quaternion PEL instance and its actual endomorphism action. Split its algebra over L and apply the selected e_i to R¹, giving rank-two summands, not raw rank-4g cohomology.
Use multiplication-by-n to isolate degree one (n prime to p), then the Young projectors on g(w−2) copies to realize the required symmetric powers and determinant exponents.
Apply the CM bridge and the a elliptic CM factors. Their selected rank-one R¹ has Tate type (−1), so the total selected direct-image degree is q₀, not the coefficient-system weight.

Only one projected Leray row survives; Saito Lemma 3 gives the displayed comparison. Choose the actual CM eigensummand before extracting H¹(−a). Rational projection does not establish a saturated integral coefficient lattice.

sources.match: The coefficient projector uses higher-dimensional quaternionic PEL powers and a CM correction, with an explicit degree shift and good-model correspondence extension.

acceptance: The raw PEL R¹, Morita summands and normalized F(k) are three distinct coefficient systems.

nodes.title: Quaternionic and inner-cohomology purity
nodes.statement: At a good proper model prime p, λ∤p, the rank-two Morita summands V_i of the genuine quaternionic PEL family are pure of geometric weight one. The raw tensor coefficient ⊗_i Sym^(n_i)V_i⊗det(V_i)^(d_i)(b) has weight r=Σ_i n_i+2Σ_i d_i−2b, hence H¹ on the proper curve has weight r+1. For Saito’s normalized F(k), the selected degree-(q₀+1) smooth proper cohomology is pure of weight q₀+1 and equals H¹(F(k))(−a); therefore H¹(F(k)) has weight q₀+1−2a=w−1, and its twist (b) has weight w−1−2b. The statement descends from G_E to G_F at places where the actual coefficient representation is unramified, by taking powers of Frobenius. For a smooth open Hilbert model and a lisse pure coefficient of weight r, its inner H_!^j=im(H_c^j→H^j) is pure of weight r+j. No whole-open-cohomology purity, bad-reduction purity or rational/integer Frobenius polynomial for an arbitrary L-projector factor is asserted.
hypotheses: Good smooth proper spreading for the indicated abelian scheme, curve and total projector variety; coefficients and projectors extend at p.
All algebraic and parity hypotheses of quaternionic-saito-projector; its CM eigensummand exists over the chosen coefficient field.
For the open Hilbert clause the actual sheaf extends as lisse pure of weight r on the chosen smooth finite-field fibre.
In the raw tensor formula n_i are nonnegative integers and d_i,b are integers; negative determinant exponents are inverse line powers over the rational coefficient field.
proofSteps: Import abelian Weil purity and the operations on pure representations to obtain the raw rank-two tensor weight; apply proper smooth direct-image/cohomology purity.

Use quaternionic-saito-projector and its good-model comparison. The selected smooth proper H^(q₀+1) has that weight; its CM factor has weight 2a. Subtract 2a and calculate (2g−1)(w−2)+1−2(g−1)(w−2)=w−1.
Use generic weights operations for the Tate twist. For descent compare Frob_u with Frob_v^f at an unramified place; the absolute values of the fth powers imply the same weight at v.
For the open Hilbert clause import DWP.7/cohomological-bounds-3-3-2-3-3-6, whose compact-support upper and ordinary-support lower bounds meet on the image.

sources.match: The projector realizes normalized coefficients with the CM twist on a good total-space model.
The two support bounds imply pure inner cohomology; proper smooth purity is their proper specialization.

acceptance: For g=2,w=4 the coefficient H¹ weight is three, not seven.
Raw coefficients and normalized F(k) must not be assigned the same weight merely because they use the same abelian family.

requests.need: Period-functor characterization of potential semistability over a specified finite extension, parallel weight-{0,1} convention, coefficient change and Weil–Deligne descent data. This imports admissibility only, not an unbuilt deformation-ring theorem.

Part II: the adjoint Selmer/dual-Selmer Taylor–Wiles selection theorem over a totally real F under MS Lemma 4.10’s two image hypotheses; chosen distinct eigenvalues at r primes with Nv≡1 mod lⁿ, and the tangent/obstruction dimension calculation producing g and dim R_loc=r+j−g+1. Existing rational Selmer kernels alone do not supply this arithmetic selection.

Part II: the finite GL₂(k_q) order-l principal-series E-model/Schur-index descent and two residual factors 1,St when q≡1 mod l; the stable lattice with trivial socle from EGS Lemma 4.1.1, and the characteristic-zero local type/Weil–Deligne computations of MS Proposition 3.10. Include the nonsplit extension orientation and inflation, without citing a downstream local Langlands roadmap.

Part II: MS Lemma 4.7’s exactness criterion for weak patching systems (MCM quotient, or residual systems with MCM residual quotient), the cofinal finite-quotient inverse-limit hypotheses, functorial type patching and augmentation. Existing free-module patching alone does not prove arbitrary exactness.

Part II: MS Lemmas 5.2–5.3 with the exact hypotheses recorded in patched-type-flatness: the X²Y→XY transfer, then the N,L²,N filtration on L⊕M with M B-flat, L=M/XM and N flat over B/(Y). Require complete local noetherian R for the second lemma and preserve all commuting R-actions.

Part II: quaternion-inner-form matching of trace distributions in the GL₂ discrete spectrum used by BR Theorem 18.1, including ramified discrete-series local character matching and the exclusion of character transfers. The generic invariant trace identity without this comparison is insufficient.
The existing AF.3 discrete cuspidal spectrum and finite-multiplicity contract, including the unitary central normalization used by the quaternionic inner-form correspondence.

The existing algebraic coefficient and rational-model contract: a common field of definition and genuine E-multiplicity spaces for the cohomological quaternionic representations. Do not infer an integral comparison from complex eigensystems.

The existing complex-points/abelian-family contract specialized to the quaternionic CM bridge of Saito §§4–6, with actual α,β maps and compatible small levels. This uses the accepted quaternionic PEL instance rather than proposing a generic PEL moduli theory.

Import the existing twisted chain/cochain and cohomology construction. Current Tau Ceti already implements the Hom-variance carrier; only the arithmetic finite-free dual/bidual comparison is new here.
Import infinitude of every Frobenius conjugacy class outside any finite set from the existing Chebotarev roadmap, not another plan of the density theorem.

Import the existing admissible narrow ray-class character/Galois character correspondence and prime-values contract. The existing Artin map is arithmetic; invert it for the declared geometric reciprocity. This is needed to globalize the two component characters in the Eisenstein-vanishing proof, not to plan class field theory again.

gaps.title: Potentially semistable deformation quotient proof
gaps.detail: MS §3.2, p.14, states the fixed-determinant potentially semistable quotient and its dimension using Kisin, Potentially semi-stable deformation rings, JAMS 21 (2008), 513–546. The original proof was not obtained/read in this pass (publisher and author endpoints refused access). Read the original representability and component-dimension proof, match the determinant θ and HT convention, and attach its exact theorem locators before proof closure. This quotient remains a mathematical construction target, not a point-condition structure assumed to be a representing ring.

gaps.title: Finite-level p-adic local compatibility for the early Hecke action
gaps.detail: MS Lemma 4.11 and §3.6 invoke EGS §6 and the finite-level p-adic compatibility input to enter the l-adic local quotient. Carayol Theorem A only covers places prime to the coefficient characteristic. Trace this weight-two finite-level compatibility proof and its semistable extension for every K_v⁰ type; do not use R22 or an R=T conclusion. The packet supplies the exact desired factorization, but this original proof chain is not closed.

sourceIssues.printed: The algebra is described as ramified at exactly one infinite place while being treated as the indefinite curve algebra.
sourceIssues.correction: Use an algebra split at exactly one real place, ramified at the other real places, with the total ramification set of even cardinality.
sourceIssues.reason: The §2.2 uniformization has one upper-half-plane factor precisely under this split-place condition. Over F=Q a real-ramified algebra is definite, so the printed condition cannot give the curve used in §6.
sourceIssues.known: No correction located; the author and journal versions inspected retain this wording.

sourceIssues.locator: §4.2, definition of the unframed fixed-determinant ring, p.23, arXiv v2
sourceIssues.printed: The unframed fixed-determinant functor uses determinant ψ, whereas the framed functor and local conditions use ψε⁻¹.
sourceIssues.correction: Both global functors use θ=ψε⁻¹, agreeing with §3’s fixed determinant and allowing the framed-to-unframed forgetful map.
sourceIssues.reason: Forgetting a frame cannot change the determinant of a lift. The two different determinant conditions would not define the asserted formally smooth forgetful map or its j=4|Σ|−1 relative dimension.
sourceIssues.known: No correction located in the versions consulted.

restructure.proposal: Keep R18.4’s target-level shape. Extend the lower-tier generic owners by the precise Part II requests above. Move only the finite-level arithmetic local deformation datum, weight-two Galois–Hecke action and quaternionic transfer input from R08/R19/R17 into this stage, so their consumers import these nodes. No R22 theorem is an input to Ihara.
restructure.reason: The integral degeneracy theorem must precede modularity lifting and its generic patching algebra already has a lower-tier owner.

upstreamNotes.note: Current Tau Ceti at a91d3aafa8cd3e6bc33dfde0d7677ed0f1625039 implements LocalCoefficientSystem.twistedCochainComplex, twistedCohomology, twistedCohomologyMap and twistedCohomologyConstantIso in Cohomology/Twisted/Basic.lean. Its linearYonedaObj is contravariant in coefficients; finite-free arithmetic W is realized using W-dual and target O. These declarations are not claimed at f790474.

R34.5/kuga-sato-projector-weight-comparison imports quaternionic geometry. The new R18.4/quaternionic-saito-projector supplies the explicit higher-dimensional PEL/CM projector and shift q0,a, without importing R34.5 back as a construction prerequisite.

The issue names H0 as the prior owner, but H0 contains no R18.4 coverage. The accepted R18.2 packet has the nine R18.4 core nodes and the precise remaining list used here. Its files are unchanged; the new early local/global bridge removes the need to cite higher tiers for this proof, with exact remaining source leaves exposed.

The pins supply fundamental-groupoid local systems and constant Z_l scheme cohomology, not the algebraic variable coefficient, derived support, integral model tower, or CM/PEL correspondence carriers. These are genuine accepted supplier/own targets; the suggested Lean omission ledger records their types in the reader. Compilation of light linear algebra does not validate those unbuilt carriers. CC.0’s constructible comparison and the accepted core retain their own stated supplier gaps. This is a carrier omission ledger, not an additional mathematical gap: construction targets are planned in the accepted core and this packet.
